extracted.intended_audience: readers of Darwin's correspondence / historians of science and naturalists
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and standards for collecting, experimenting, measuring, and reporting empirical natural-history data (specimens, seeds, breeding observations) as illustrated in Darwin's correspondence and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive collection and balanced treatment of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: to view all facts that I can master ... to see how far they favour or are opposed to the notion that wild species are mutable or immutable: I mean with my utmost power to give all arguments and facts on both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather as complete a body of evidence as possible and present both supporting and opposing arguments; strive for balance rather than selective citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual measurement and arithmetic rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: I have no faith in anything short of actual measurement and the Rule of Three.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative measurement (weights, proportions, lengths) and simple arithmetic rules to compare specimens objectively rather than relying on impressionistic judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative anatomy and systematic measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: I am making skeletons... comparing wild and tame ducks... the proportional weights of the two have greatly varied... I find the tame-duck wing ought... to have its two wings 360 grains in weight, but it has it only 317.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare corresponding structures across wild and domestic forms, prepare skeletons or cleaned specimens, and record proportional/absolute measurements to detect morphological changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled, repeatable experiments (seed immersion and germination)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have in small bottles out of doors, exposed to variation of temperature, cress, radish, cabbages, lettuces... after immersion for exactly one week, have all germinated... I replant the same seeds as above after fourteen days' immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments with clear treatments (e.g., immersion durations), environmental control/variation, replication, and re-testing (replanting after set intervals) to establish repeatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record specimen provenance and exact age
rubrics_metrics.description: I should therefore be very glad for a seven-days' duckling and for one of the old birds, should one ever die a natural death... I would beg a chicken with exact age stated, about a week or fortnight old!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require and record precise provenance information (age, origin, breeder notes) for specimens used in developmental or comparative studies, since age affects the traits measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen killing, preservation, and shipping procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The way I shall kill young things will be to put them under a tumbler glass with a teaspoon of ether or chloroform... the best way would be to send them as you procure them, in pasteboard chip-box by post... just tie up with string; and you will REALLY make me happier by allowing me to keep an account of postage, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practical methods for humane killing (ether/chloroform or cyanide as described historically), pack specimens in suitable containers for postal transport, label/address parcels clearly, and keep records of postage and handling. (Note: these historical methods reflect 19th-century practice.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collaborative networks and many helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: I have a NUMBER of people helping me in every way, and giving me most valuable assistance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlist a distributed network of correspondents and local collectors to obtain diverse specimens and observations that would be impractical for one person to gather alone; value and acknowledge their contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report absolute counts as well as proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: it would be advisable for botanists to give in WHOLE NUMBERS, as well as in the lowest fraction, the proportional numbers of the families
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting botanical (or other categorical) comparisons, provide whole counts alongside fractional/proportional figures so readers can judge the robustness of comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect editorial precedence and choose appropriate venues
rubrics_metrics.description: As the 'Gardeners' Chronicle' put in my question, and took notice of it, I think I am bound to send, which I had thought of doing next week, my first report to Lindley... When my experiments are ended (should the results appear worthy) and should the 'Linnean Journal' not object to the previous publication of imperfect and provisional reports, I should be DELIGHTED to insert the final report there
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer preliminary reports to appropriate, possibly more popular outlets but consult and give first option to relevant editors; aim to publish definitive results in the proper scholarly journal if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about unwarranted assumptions; consider alternative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: I find that he coolly assumes, (1) that formerly insects possessed greater migratory powers than now, (2) that the old land was SPECIALLY rich in centres of creation, (3) that the uniting land was destroyed before the special creations had time to diffuse, and (4) that the land was broken down before certain families and genera had time to reach... Are not these a jolly lot of assumptions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid accepting untested background assumptions; explicitly list and question alternative suppositions that could explain the same data before drawing strong conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term and patient data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: I have been collecting facts for these dozen years... I have a NUMBER of people helping me in every way...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some research questions require many years of observation and accumulation of facts; be prepared for long-term effort and incremental progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimic natural variation in experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: I have in small bottles out of doors, exposed to variation of temperature... I filled a great tank with snow... seeds in salt water immersed in water of 32-33 degrees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing ecological or biogeographical hypotheses, expose samples to realistic environmental variation (temperature swings, realistic salinity) rather than only constant laboratory conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate specimens for the question
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall make my skeletons of old cocks... I do not care for a baby turkey, nor for a mastiff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose specimen types and life stages that best serve the measurement or comparative objective (e.g., adult/old individuals for skeletal comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specimen lists and classificatory detail to collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: If my success seems to make it worth while, I will send a seed list, to get you to mark some different classes of seeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply collaborators and correspondents with detailed specimen lists and classification schemes to standardize identifications and facilitate comparative tabulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enthusiasm, close observation, and attention to detail in breeding/variety studies
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a good breeder, and to succeed in improving any breed, beyond everything enthusiasm is required... the extreme attention and close observation necessary to be a good fancier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful breeding and variety studies require sustained enthusiasm and meticulous attention to multiple small characteristic traits rather than attempting to attend to all possible features at once.
